x.author: kedytcom
x.body:
The problem could be what happens before users see the offer.

A strong first-time experience usually follows a simple sequence:

1-Explain the outcome clearly.
2-Show the most valuable benefits.
3-Ask users a relevant question.
4-Personalize the experience.
5-Present the premium offer.

Users need to understand what your app can do for them before deciding whether it is worth paying for.

Don’t sell “premium access.”

Sell the result:

❌ Unlock all features
✅ Create professional videos in minut

x.author: patiencebuilds
x.body:
The best audit of a tool is a few days without it.

The navigation app dies on a back road. The spreadsheet will not open. The power goes out at the workshop. The assistant you lean on every day goes dark. Within hours, two things become clear at once.

The first is how dependent you had become, and how fast. The discomfort is the measurement. Things that were supposed to be conveniences turn out to be load-bearing.

The second is what still works. The skill. The judgment. The relationships. Som
